items.name: O2 Academy Brixton
items.description: A legendary 5,000-capacity Art Deco venue, originally a 1920s cinema, that became a full-time music venue in 1983. Hosted David Bowie, Bob Dylan, Amy Winehouse, and Nirvana among countless others.

items.name: Barbican Centre
items.description: Europe's largest arts centre and a landmark of brutalist architecture, hosting classical and contemporary concerts alongside art, film and design events. Past performers include Damon Albarn and Nick Cave.

items.name: Union Chapel
items.description: A working Grade II-listed church transformed into one of London's most atmospheric live music venues, with genuinely stunning acoustics. Hosts intimate acoustic sets and full bands alike.

items.name: MOTH Club
items.description: A former working men's social club turned beloved indie gig venue, known for its gold-tinsel-lined back room and reliably excellent line-ups of up-and-coming acts.

items.name: Royal Festival Hall
items.description: Home to the London Philharmonic Orchestra within the Southbank Centre, hosting formal classical concerts alongside a broad contemporary programme year-round.

items.name: Hammersmith Apollo
items.description: A historic 5,000-capacity venue that's gone by several names over the decades, hosting major touring acts across rock, pop and comedy in a grand Art Deco setting.

items.name: Alexandra Palace
items.description: A historic North London venue with sweeping city views, having hosted Suede, Blur, The White Stripes and the Stone Roses. One of the largest indoor concert spaces in the capital.

items.name: The Windmill Brixton
items.description: A no-frills, much-loved pub venue for rough-and-ready rock and indie gigs, credited with launching several of London's most talked-about new bands.

items.name: Wilton's Music Hall
items.description: The world's oldest surviving grand music hall, dating to 1859, with a beautifully weathered interior that's hosted everyone from opera to contemporary gigs. A genuinely unique London venue.

items.name: O2 Forum Kentish Town
items.description: A converted Art Deco cinema turned mid-size music venue, hosting major touring bands and club nights in North London. One of the city's most atmospheric medium-capacity spaces.

items.name: O2 Shepherd's Bush Empire
items.description: A historic 1903 theatre turned major West London music venue, hosting some of the biggest touring gigs and club nights outside the West End.

items.name: The Old Blue Last
items.description: A Shoreditch pub venue with live music and DJs most nights of the week, many shows free to attend. A launching pad for emerging indie and alternative acts.

items.name: The Lexington
items.description: An Islington pub venue known for rock and indie gigs upstairs and a basement space with more of a blues vibe, plus a serious bourbon selection at the bar.
